subject: Civil Engineering
title: The Vajont Dam Disaster
description: A quick win: understand The Vajont Dam Disaster.

hook.text: The dam survived perfectly. The mountain behind it collapsed into the reservoir — killing 2,000.

buildup.text: In 1963, a massive landslide dropped 260 million cubic meters of rock into Italy's Vajont reservoir.

discovery.text: The displaced water overtopped the dam by 250 meters — a mega-tsunami in a mountain valley.

twist.text: Engineers had detected slope movement for years — but underestimated the landslide volume.

climax.text: The dam still stands today — undamaged. The failure was in understanding the environment.

punchline.text: The dam was perfect. The mountain was the danger. Wrong valley, right dam.

quiz.question: What caused the Vajont Dam disaster despite the dam itself being undamaged?
options: An earthquake cracked the dam's foundation and released the reservoir
A massive landslide displaced reservoir water over the dam, creating a catastrophic flood
Heavy rainfall caused the reservoir to overflow the dam crest naturally

details.summary: The Vajont Dam disaster of 1963 in Italy killed nearly 2,000 people when a massive landslide of 270 million cubic meters plunged into the reservoir, generating a 250-meter-high wave that overtopped the dam and destroyed the town of Longarone below. The dam itself survived intact.
details.whyItMatters: Vajont is the most devastating dam-related disaster caused by reservoir-induced landslide. It demonstrated that dam safety must consider the entire reservoir environment, not just the dam structure itself.
takeaways: A 270 million cubic meter landslide displaced the reservoir water over the dam
The resulting wave was 250 meters high, far exceeding the dam's 262-meter height
The dam structure itself did not fail, proving the disaster was geological

faq.question: Were there warning signs before the Vajont landslide?
faq.answer: Yes. Slope movements had been detected for three years, with creep rates accelerating as reservoir levels rose. A smaller landslide had occurred in 1960.

faq.question: What lessons did the engineering profession learn from Vajont?
faq.answer: Vajont established that reservoir slopes must be thoroughly investigated for landslide potential before and during filling. Dam safety must encompass the entire reservoir environment. Warning signs from monitoring must trigger decisive action.
